solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Candy store folds by spring (4,4)

blocks.note: tucks are folds sewn into cloth
to hop is to spring

annotation.surface: A sweet shop's paper bags are folded up beside a spring display.
annotation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school's snack and sweet shop; 'tuck' is schoolboy slang for food. The wordplay split falls one letter off the (4,4) break.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional equivalent: British 'tuck' is sweets and snacks, which Americans call candy.

entries.clue: Coastal feature that grows economy (6)

blocks.note: a coastal plant, the sea pink, growing on cliffs and salt marshes
economy in the sense of careful spending

annotation.surface: Something on the coast is boosting the economy, like a seaside resort.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'grows economy' as one phrase about a booming coast; the split falls after 'grows', and 'feature that grows' is simply a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: thrift is the sea pink of coastal cliffs, and also frugality.

entries.clue: Supply column tracked vehicle (11)

blocks.note: to cater is to supply food
a pillar is a column

annotation.surface: A military supply column made up of tracked vehicles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply column' reads as one military phrase, but it splits into two pieces of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A trademark turned generic: Caterpillar tracks gave their name to any vehicle running on continuous tracks, like a bulldozer.

entries.clue: Spread most of the crumbs (7)

indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: to strew is to scatter or spread
THE without its last letter

annotation.surface: Scattering most of the breadcrumbs, perhaps for the birds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' looks like bread; it is the mild British exclamation of surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; strewth is a squashed 'God's truth'.

entries.clue: Approach from both sides of exterior (5)

indicatorNotes.both sides of: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: off = from, as in 'take it off the shelf'
first and last letters of EXTERIOR

annotation.surface: Coming at a building from both sides of its exterior.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Approach' looks like movement towards a place; here it is a proposal, as in making an approach to a buyer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: making an approach to someone is putting a proposal to them.

entries.clue: Siren’s short catchphrase (6)

indicatorNotes.short: short means cut off at the end

blocks.note: a siren, a woman who lures men, is a mantrap
MANTRAP loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A seductive woman's trademark line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Siren's' reads as possessive; the 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition. A mantrap is a dangerously alluring woman.
annotation.definitionFit: An extended sense: a mantra, first a repeated prayer, is now any phrase someone repeats constantly.

entries.clue: One in a tank or one in an aircraft (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one letter goes in another word

blocks.note: A + VAT, a vat is a tank
I is the Roman one, placed inside AVAT
taken as written

annotation.surface: A choice between a tank crew and an aircraft crew.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets a tank against a plane as two military postings; the first 'one' is wordplay, and only the second half of the clue defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an aviator flies aircraft, so is one found in an aircraft.

entries.clue: Upturned egg container (3)

indicatorNotes.Upturned: in a down entry, turning it up writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: a nit is a louse egg

annotation.surface: A boiled egg turned upside down in an eggcup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Egg container' reads as an eggcup or box, but the words split: egg is wordplay, and container defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tins hold food, paint and so on.

entries.clue: Hearing car, try to cross over (8)

indicatorNotes.to cross: TRY crosses, or straddles, the O

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

annotation.surface: Hearing a car coming and trying to cross the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a verb; it is the adjective, as in a hearing aid.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival sense: 'hearing' as in hearing loss or a hearing test concerns the auditory sense.

entries.clue: Lily Allen’s first LP eh? Sod off (8)

indicatorNotes.off: off as in gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of ALLEN
anagram fodder LPEHSOD

annotation.surface: A rude reaction to a pop singer's debut album.
annotation.walkthrough: Lily Allen is a British pop singer, so 'Lily' looks like her first name; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the asphodel belongs to the lily family, the flower of the Greek underworld.

entries.clue: Turner’s corrupt men (5)

blocks.note: to rot is to corrupt
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: The painter Turner's dissolute male companions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turner' with a capital looks like the painter J M W Turner; it is anything that turns, and the 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading: the rotor is the part of a machine that turns.

entries.clue: Made a “thing” to pen his new single (9)

indicatorNotes.to pen: a pen encloses, so FAD holds the rest
indicatorNotes.new: his made new, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: a 'thing' is a craze
HIS rearranged
single = one

annotation.surface: A pop star turns his new single into a big event.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag 'thing' in its slang sense, the latest craze; 'single' looks like a record but is just a number.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something fashioned by hand has been made or shaped.

entries.clue: Texas city couple run away to hide this (4,5)

indicatorNotes.to hide this: FORTH hides 'this', the couple and run before it

blocks.note: to go forth is to go away
a couple is two
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

annotation.surface: A pair flee a Texas city to hide something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple run away' reads as eloping, but 'couple run' is what gets hidden and 'away' does the hiding; 'this' points back to it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Fort Worth is one of the large cities of Texas, next to Dallas.

entries.clue: Plot of short written work (5)

blocks.note: plot in the sense of a piece of land
a pamphlet or brief treatise, often religious

annotation.surface: The storyline of a short story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a storyline next to 'written work'; it is a plot of land.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tract is a stretch of land and also a short treatise.

entries.clue: Caught her up, put on manacles (11)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up writes the word bottom to top
indicatorNotes.manacles: put on shackles her, holding REH inside

blocks.note: to append is to put on, add
HER written backwards

annotation.surface: Police caught a woman and put her in handcuffs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put on manacles' reads as handcuffing; 'put on' is one piece and 'manacles' is the instruction to enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: police who apprehend a suspect catch or arrest them.

entries.clue: Correct graph, printed or otherwise (5,3,6)

indicatorNotes.otherwise: in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Checking whether a graph is right, on paper or on screen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'printed or otherwise' as a stock phrase; 'or' is fodder and 'otherwise' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'right and proper' is a set phrase meaning correct and fitting, as in 'it is only right and proper'.

entries.clue: Thumping a Liberal could end in injury (8)

indicatorNotes.end in: the end of injury is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
L = Liberal
might = could
last letter of INJURY

annotation.surface: Punching a politician could leave someone hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thumping' looks like hitting; it is the informal adjective for huge, as in 'a thumping majority'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonyms: a thumping row and an almighty row are both enormous ones.

entries.clue: Last, despite what is expected (5,3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Last' works as an adverb: to finish last is to finish behind the rest.

blocks.note: finishing behind everyone else
in spite of expectations, as in 'it rained in the end'

annotation.surface: Someone finishes last against the odds.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is read literally: what comes last comes behind every other thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally following everything else, and idiomatically 'contrary to what was expected'.

entries.clue: Game full of action replays (6,2,6)

blocks.note: the surface suggests a sports match being televised
read literally: every action one player makes is repeated by the others

annotation.surface: A sports match shown with plenty of television replays.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Action replays' points at televised sport; in this children's game the line of players copies whatever the one at the front does.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: in this children's game each player copies, or replays, the moves of the one in front.

entries.clue: Giant in old hat exhales audibly (7)

indicatorNotes.audibly: as heard, so the sound of a word stands for another spelling

blocks.note: old hat means out of fashion, out
sighs and size sound the same

annotation.surface: A giant wearing an old hat breathes out heavily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Giant in old hat' paints a figure in headgear; 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay, and 'old hat' is one idea, meaning unfashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjectival synonyms: outsize clothes are for unusually large, giant sizes.

entries.clue: A story — a funny one — almost repeated (3,4)

indicatorNotes.almost repeated: the phrase comes again without its last letter

blocks.note: A, then 'a gas', informal for something very funny
the previous piece again, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A story told with one funny bit that nearly comes round twice.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga saga is a British genre of novel about comfortable country families; an Aga is a range cooker found in such kitchens.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Aga saga is a kind of story, a novel of middle-class rural life.

entries.clue: Somewhat unfair, one recruits evening worker (6)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the letters, a run inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of unfair, all of 'one' and the start of recruits

annotation.surface: A slightly unfair policy of one firm hiring night-shift staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evening worker' reads as a night-shift employee; it is someone who makes things even, smoothing creases.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: pressing clothes evens them out, so the presser is literally an evening worker.

entries.clue: Bird baster gets stuffing back (5)

indicatorNotes.stuffing: the answer is the stuffing inside the words
indicatorNotes.back: back as in backwards, so the hidden letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: bas(TER GE)ts

annotation.surface: A cook bastes a roast bird and stuffs it.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen words all point at a roast bird, but the bird sits backwards inside 'baster gets'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the egret is a small white heron, so a bird.

entries.clue: Daring to capture aged Irish former PM (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to capture: GAME captures OLD, holding it inside

blocks.note: game = plucky, daring
aged = old
IR = Irish

annotation.surface: A bold raid to seize an elderly Irish ex-premier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irish former PM' looks like a Taoiseach; Irish is only IR, and the former PM is Israel's.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Golda Meir was Prime Minister of Israel from 1969 to 1974.

entries.clue: Where to get drink without sugar? (5)

annotation.definition: Where to get drink without sugar?

blocks.note: a straight reading: the neighbourhood pub
split the answer as low-cal, short for low-calorie, a drink with no sugar

annotation.surface: Asking where to buy a sugar-free drink.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain your local is your regular neighbourhood pub; broken in two, the word reads as a sugar-free 'lo-cal' label.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: the British 'local' is your regular pub, and said as lo-cal it describes a sugar-free drink.

entries.clue: Not believing fellow is in loft (9)

indicatorNotes.in: in as in inside, so the words before it go inside the loft

blocks.note: a loft is an attic
a fellow is a he
taken as written

annotation.surface: A sceptical man is up in the loft, like a hermit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fellow is' reads as a verb phrase, but the two words are separate pieces that drop into the loft.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be atheistic is to have no belief in God.

entries.clue: Half of us are smelly (3)

indicatorNotes.Half of: keep half the letters of the word

blocks.note: us, the human race
the first three of six letters

annotation.surface: A rude joke that half the group smell.
annotation.walkthrough: To hum is British slang for to smell bad; 'are smelly' is a plural verb, matching 'they hum'.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: things that hum give off a bad smell.

entries.clue: Notice, and dress in, accessory (3,2)

blocks.note: an ad is a notice
to don is to dress in

annotation.surface: Spot it, and wear it, the finishing touch to an outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fashion advice about spotting something and wearing it; 'notice' here is a small advertisement.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an extra fitted to something, as an accessory is.

entries.clue: Ignoring cold, mountaineer is able to move supply (6)

indicatorNotes.Ignoring: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the C for cold is dropped

blocks.note: a mountaineer is a climber
C = cold, as on a tap; removed

annotation.surface: A climber manages without heating to shift supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as provisions; it is the adverb of supple, so 'able to move supply' means flexible.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: limber and supple both describe a body that bends freely.

entries.clue: Ornamental ring beloved of Hero (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Ornamental' is used as a noun: an ornamental plant.

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero

annotation.surface: A decorative ring belonging to a heroic figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hero' looks like any hero; here she is the priestess Hero, and 'Ornamental' is a noun for a plant grown for show.
annotation.definitionFit: Gardeners' usage: an ornamental is a plant grown for looks, and the oleander is a showy flowering shrub.
